description: The Wood Dog in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1934 and 1994 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Dog is the Dog born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the eleventh animal. It combines the Dog's loyalty with Wood's qualities. Wood Dog years between 1924 and 2044 are 1934 and 1994. The Dog's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Wood Dog personality
paragraphs: Wood controls Earth, and the Dog's fixed element is Earth, so a Wood stem is said to stir the Dog's steady core, opening it towards growth, cooperation and broader causes. Wood Dogs are commonly pictured as warm, idealistic and fair-minded, loyal to friends and committed to doing right by the wider community. They tend to be more trusting and easy-going than other Dogs, and often enjoy collaborative work. Their sense of justice is strong, and they may champion people who are overlooked. The stirring influence keeps them engaged, though it can also create inner unease, with Wood's push to expand clashing against the Dog's caution and protective instincts. Few signs are as willing to share a burden.

In the five-element scheme, Wood belongs to the east and to the green energy of early spring, and that seasonal image shapes how it colours an animal sign. A Wood stem tends to soften sharp edges and add warmth, curiosity and a cooperative instinct. Traditional texts associate it with benevolence, growth and the wish to build something that lasts beyond the self. People born under a Wood stem are often portrayed as principled, open-handed and hopeful about others. The caution usually attached to Wood is a habit of spreading energy thinly, saying yes to every request and feeling quietly hurt when generosity is not returned in kind.

sections.heading: Wood Dog at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

Warm, fair and cooperative, the Wood Dog is frequently called the conscience of a team. Social work, teaching, advocacy, human resources and charity management are commonly suggested, since a sense of justice and a talent for collaboration matter there. It works best when the mission is worthy and colleagues share its values. In love, the Wood Dog is loyal, generous and protective, always ready to answer the phone at any hour. Trust and integrity in a partner are non-negotiable for it. Overcommitment is the familiar danger here: it may take on too many people's troubles and become anxious or drained.

sections.heading: Wood Dog years and dates
paragraphs: Wood Dog years in the Lunar New Year table run from February 14, 1934 to February 3, 1935 and from February 10, 1994 to January 30, 1995. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1934 anyone born before Feb 14 is a Water Rooster, not a Wood Dog. Sixty years separate each Wood Dog year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Wood Dog year is Yang, matching the Dog's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Jia-Xu: Jia is the yang Wood stem and Xu is the Dog's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Water Rooster year (before February 14, 1934) and the Water Rooster year (before February 10, 1994), and births in the weeks after each Wood Dog year ends belong to the Wood Pig. The new year itself fell on a Wednesday in 1934 and Thursday in 1994.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Dog
paragraphs: Wood Dogs often benefit from directing their loyalty towards a few well-chosen causes rather than many. That focus helps their idealism make a visible difference. Because they trust generously, checking new commitments carefully protects them from disappointment. Wood Dogs may also worry more than they admit, and talking through concerns with a trusted friend eases the burden. Collaborative outdoor activities, such as community gardening or team sports, satisfy both their sociability and need for purpose. When their fairness is paired with discernment, Wood Dogs become trusted champions and true friends.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Dog shares the Dog's San He trine with the Tiger and Horse (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Rabbit, and its Liu Chong clash with the Dragon. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Dog years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1934 (from February 14, 1934) and 1994 (from February 10, 1994). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Dog's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Dog's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles wood controls Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Dog?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Tiger and Horse (San He) and the Rabbit (Liu He). The Dragon is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Dog called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Jia-Xu. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Jia, followed by its earthly branch, here Xu for the Dog, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Dog different from other Dogs?
faq.answer: All Dogs share loyalty, fairness and protectiveness. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
